# Native dependency provenance

JNI bridge `app/src/main/cpp/llama_jni.cpp` and `logging.h` are adapted from OpenBMB/MiniCPM-V-Apps commit `d0dd7a6074b950081d6303977efb646f2f85bb5b`, MIT license in MiniCPM-LICENSE. Changes: temperature 0.1, clearing freed native pointers/batch to support repeated imports and releases, and raising a Java exception if context reset fails. Kotlin downloader/UI code is not included.

Engine: `tc-mb/llama.cpp-omni`, commit `e0eca9d8f57ac8f5a5ad6191a8007b93436c1e71`, the official demo's gitlink at the commit above. Downloaded archive SHA-256: `3ce1d3938dcd52561295253eac8708311cff2996c6a4b34982353fe832f9a195`. Kept outside Git; prepare_engine.py verifies the pinned archive then applies patch_engine.py. The patch guards two Darwin-only F_NOCACHE hints that otherwise fail to compile on Android. It does not change the dense 1B model's inference. The engine and bundled dependencies retain their own license files.

Full APK builds optionally bundle MiniCPM-V 4.7 1B Q4_K_M and its matching f16 vision projector. These weights are excluded from Git and from lite builds. Their publisher declares Apache-2.0 in the pinned model card; `model-specs/minicpm-1b.json` records the publisher repository revision, exact weight sizes and SHA-256 hashes, license declaration URL, and a pinned copy of the publisher's Apache-2.0 text. The full APK includes that license and provenance in `assets/local-ai/`. The JNI software's MIT license does not license the model weights.
